newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait allocates $330mln to help small businesses.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait allocates $330mln to help small businesses.

text.p: Kuwait has created a $330 million firm to help investors launch small national industrial concerns, the Kuwait News Agency reported on Tuesday.

Small Projects Development Co (SPDC) " will manage a portfolio worth 100 million dinars ($330 million) to develop the economy...and encourage individual business initiatives," it reported SPDC chairman Adnan al-Sultan as saying.

"Among the objectives of the company is to create work openings for Kuwaiti youth," he said. "That comes form encouraging individual initiatives of Kuwait's youth to execute projects complementing medium and major industries."
Sultan said the firm was established by the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, to also improve and boost services in Kuwait and develop a specialised native workforce.
He did not give further details.
KIA, overseeing the state's privatisation plan, is trying to create alternative private sector jobs for Kuwaiti workers.
Parliamentarians have expressed concern that selling off state services to the private sector would result in layoffs.
